input:
A centrifugal pump moves caustic solution between two vessels at grade, and its duty point is a flow of 71 m3 h-1 against a head of 44 m. At the duty point the pump efficiency is 81% and the shaft power is 10.5 kW. The motor is rated 15% above the duty-point shaft power, so the installed motor carries a margin over the 10.5 kW the pump draws at the duty point, and the margin is a property of the motor selection rather than of the pump curve.

The four duty figures belong together. Flow and head fix the duty point on the pump's characteristic; efficiency states what fraction of the shaft power reaches the liquid at that point; and the shaft power is the demand the motor has to meet. A change in any one of them moves the duty point, and the remaining figures then describe a different operating state, not the one tested.

Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test. The test ran for 4 h at the duty point only, and the detection statement is bounded by that scope: cavitation is excluded at the duty point over the duration of the test, and the test states nothing about cavitation at flows above or below the duty point, or over longer runs. The duty figures and the cavitation statement are therefore single-point results, valid at the stated duty point, and they are the basis for acceptance.
